newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki bull-run resumes after US wage data.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki bull-run resumes after US wage data.

text.p: Finnish shares reversed losses and ended well in positive territory on Tuesday after a lower-than-forecast rise in U.S. fourth quarter employment costs boosted international bond and stock markets, brokers said.
Technical problems delayed the opening by over two hours and brokers said this helped cap losses ahead of the recovery.
The HEX jumped 1.06 percent to close at 2,735.99 points and volume was lively at almost 600 million markka despite the loss of two trading hours, with a third in bourse engine Nokia.
The benign U.S. wage report spread hopes that the Federal Reserve would not raise interest rates at its meeting next week.
Insurer Pohjola shrugged off Moody's comment late on Monday that it may consider an insurance rating downgrade, ending sharply higher at 147.00, up 8.00 markka or almost six percent.
Nokia rose 3.00 markka to 313.00. It opened higher in New York but did not reach the equivalent of 313.00 markka in early Wall Steet dealings.
Hardware and car retailer Starckjohann was very lively, adding 0.50 markka or 6.41 percent on the company's positive earnings outlook, brokers said.
"A few brokerages have issued upbeat reports on Starckjohann," said one.
Compass maker Suunto looked firm after two large in-house deals but ended flat at 55.00 markka.
